training_scope: New training is confined to the new benchmarks in this namespace: the E3 development cohort, the 1e4/1e5 budget controls, the 24-fit E3 held-out cohort, the E6 centres across three architectures, and the E6/E7 shared centre cache. No historical PINN was retrained and no historical seed was replaced.
notes: E0 reproduces every paper-facing statistic from the frozen tag; 370x and 73x are ratios of medians, not medians of paired ratios.

E1 verifies H_ll - G_ll = diag(g_l) and H_aa - G_aa = 0 on ten real two-parameter checkpoints by autograd, and validates the adapter by regenerating archived collocation points bit-exactly and by reproducing the historical F_raw, F_se and H_red.
The E1 identity does not require stationarity: seeds 219 and 221 passing it does not conflict with their historical invalid labels, and they must not enter the accuracy queue.

E2 scalar queue NOT_AVAILABLE (no state tensors). The two-parameter post-hoc run met its objective but the previous wording (small gradient implies large state error) was an over-claim and has been corrected to a sensitivity statement.

E2 curvature drift: over the eight valid centres the exact reference drifts by 0.013%-6.9% of the SAEPS error, and the method ordering never changes. The wording is bounded to 'stable over the tested refinement range'.
E3 preflight passes fully, and the non-affine identity H - G - g = kappa^2 sum r d2r/dkappa2 holds exactly, with the non-affine term (-42.54) comparable in size to the log-gradient term (+38.74).

E3 blocker resolved at development stage: the exact reduction failed for 8/8 fits because the 1000-iteration state polish left the state non-stationary. The polish budget was raised to 30000 on a stationarity and budget-completeness criterion recorded in protocol.yaml development_change_log. No clamping and no damping substitution was applied.

E3 development at 30000: 8/8 pass the exact reduction, SAEPS wins 8/8, median E_raw 16.16 against median E_SAEPS 1.19e-3 (about 1.35e4x), median kappa relative error 1.19%, and the non-affine identity holds to 8.0e-15 on the real fits.
E3 error decomposition: E_fix is as bad as E_raw, so the improvement comes entirely from the state-elimination relaxation term, which GN reproduces to E_relax = 5.5e-6.

E3 budget convergence: the cohort median E_SAEPS moves 7.7% then 2.2% across budgets 1e4/3e4/1e5, and 5 of 8 fits change by under 1% between 3e4 and 1e5; the worst single fit still moves 14.2%, so cohort statistics are near-converged while per-fit absolute values retain a disclosed sensitivity.
Final E3 budget set to 1e5 on stationarity and convergence-trend grounds only; SAEPS wins 8/8 at every budget tested.
E3 protocol frozen in reports/E3_FROZEN_PROTOCOL.json with SHA256 of protocol.yaml and src/e3_saturation.py. The held-out runner fails closed if the snapshot is missing, mismatched or unauthorized.

E3 held-out (frozen 1e5) is complete and confirms development on fresh data seeds: 24/24 fits valid, 6/6 data seeds complete, no exclusions, SAEPS wins 24/24 with a one-sided sign-test p of 5.96e-08. Median E_raw 16.8165 against median E_SAEPS 1.0603e-3; R1 (ratio of medians) 15860 and R2 (median paired ratio) 13257 are both reported because they differ. Median kappa relative error 1.15%. The decomposition repeats the development mechanism: median E_fix 16.8177 is as bad as E_raw, so the gain comes from the state-elimination relaxation term, which GN reproduces to E_relax 1.3e-05. Noise does not weaken it (12/12 wins at both levels).

E4: all 80 required checks pass across 10 centres. The param-coordinate Gauss-Newton reduction is equivariant to 2.0e-12, while the exact reduced Hessian needs the diag(a*g_a) term and the naive form fails by 0.44%-4.9%. Keeping the metric T^T T leaves the reduced curvature invariant (<=9.2e-11) whereas the identity metric does not, and invariance is deliberately not required there. No claim of invariance under arbitrary reparameterisation.

E5: 8/8 valid centres have resolved weak directions (relative eigengap 0.82-0.93 against a 0.1 threshold), in a pre-declared Euclidean metric on the log coefficients rather than the whitened space. Median angle to the exact weak direction is 0.45 degrees for SAEPS against 2.86 degrees for raw. Exact curvature is positive definite at all 8, so no negative-curvature sign report was needed. The boundary is stated: local diagnostic only, no claim of improved parameter recovery.

E8: 72 runs at a matched gamma (all methods share one gamma per level), zero initial guess, one discarded warm-up and three timed repeats per condition; every status PASS. CG's cost falls about 17x as alpha rises from 1e-8 to 1e-2 (10.63 s to 0.60 s, 650 to 29 iterations) while scaled LSQR's cost is nearly flat (143.9 s to 98.9 s, 4300 to 3118 iterations). LSQR costs 14-150x more than CG but is 4 orders more accurate at the weakest damping (1.19e-12 against 2.99e-08). The preconditioner build is under 1% of the LSQR total, so the iterations, not the preparation, are the expensive stage. Peak native tensor memory is not claimed and the optional large-scale operator timing was not run.

E8 also exposed a real implementation error caught by comparing against the historical record: the refined LSQR helper's Fse is already the reduced value, not a correction to subtract from F_raw. The wrong assembly gave a 17.2 relative error against the dense solve and would have been reported as 'LSQR fails at weak damping'; the corrected assembly gives 1.19e-12, matching the historical 1.47e-12. This is why the E0-style source cross-check earns its place.

E6 completes the plan: three genuinely trained architectures on the same data, noise and initializations. All 18 centres have a valid exact reduction (6/6 for each of n=65, n=129, n=337), SAEPS wins 18/18, and the median E_SAEPS improves with size from 9.224e-4 to 6.087e-4 to 4.322e-4, so the advantage is not an artifact of the compact network. The mechanism is unchanged (median E_fix equals E_raw, E_GN_fix about 0.944, E_relax about 1e-5). Median training time is not monotone: 272 s, 526 s, 371 s. The assembled state Hessian matches an independent HVP to 1.5e-15 at the largest architecture. Labeled a preplanned paired architecture extension with independent_confirmation false; it does not revise the historical width-32 result, which remains 0/5 valid.

E7 four-level scope, from existing records: COMPUTABLE 21/21 steps; STATIONARITY_RESOLVED 0/21, since no step reaches the tightest tolerance on both sides and only 5 of 126 refinements reach any graded tolerance; BRANCH_COMPARABLE 21/21; REFERENCE_AGREEMENT 20/21 within 10 percent. So the defensible claim is numerical consistency at a fixed anchor and damping, NOT a strictly converged independent profile check. Proximity to the Schur reference is deliberately not used to define comparability, which would be circular.

L-BFGS stop-reason audit complete. In torch 2.13.0+cpu max_eval defaults to max_iter*5//4 and the loop breaks on current_evals >= max_eval before the gradient or change tolerances. 27 of the 30 E2 records were bound by the FUNCTION-EVALUATION budget (closure calls 1251 against max_eval 1250, n_iter only 625), so the old budget_exhausted flag reported False misleadingly; three records (seed 220) stopped below both budgets and the records cannot identify which condition fired. An instrumented reproduction of the same configuration bound on the ITERATION budget instead, so the binding constraint must not be generalised between cases. E3/E6/E7 recorded only accepted iterations, so their stop reason is UNKNOWN and was not reconstructed by re-running.
